PURPOSE:  To consider  a request  to install  a new wireless  telecommunications  facility  on the
rooftop  of an existing  apartment  structure  located  at 8633 California  Avenue  (APNNo.  6210-018-
056).

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:

  a.  CONDUCT  a public  hearing;

  b.  ACCEPT  the Class 3 Categorical  Exemption  from  the California  Environtnental  Quality
  Act ("CEQA"),  codified  at Division  6 of Title  14 of the California  Code of Regulations.  A

  small  structures;  and the conversion  of existing  small  structures  from  one use to another

GENERAL INFORMATION Staff has completed a review of the subject application and
determined that the proposed Conditional Use Permit No. 864 is in compliance with the City of
South Gate’s Zoning Code and General Plan

Background
The subject property is zoned CC (Civic Center) and is located on California Avenue, south of
Ardmore Avenue and north of Firestone Boulevard. The property falls within the Civic Center
District of the General Plan.

The subject property is developed as a residential apartment building with multiple units, in
addition to multiple commercial units located on the ground level of the structure. The structure
totals approximately 55,723 square feet in size, four floors and 69 residential and commercial units.

Conditional Use Permit
Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section 11.21.030 “Land use permissions

  8
 tables”, Conditional Use Permits are required to be reviewed and approved for
“Antenna/Communications Equipment” in the Civic Center zone.

The proposed application includes the installation of antenna screens, panel antennas, jumpers,
RRUs (remote radio units), surge suppression devices, power cables, fiber cables, an equipment
cabinet, power conduit, etc. This equipment would be installed within existing screened areas on
the rooftop of the existing apartment structure. The project provides stealth screening which allows
the proposed antennas to be utilized, while they are also completely screened from view.
Conditions of approval contained within Resolution No. 2023-03 also provide for additional
architectural accents to ensure that the proposed project conforms with the existing structure and
architectural elements.

Conditional Use Permit Findings
The findings for Conditional Use Permit No. 864 are provided below:

  1. Approval of the CUP is consistent with and will not adversely affect the intent and purpose
  of this title or the city’s general plan.
  The subject property is zoned Civic Center (CC) and is located within the Civic Center
  District of the General Plan. Therefore, the subject project must comply with the
  regulations set forth in the South Gate Municipal Code and General Plan.

  2. The design and development of the land use and conditions of the CUP are compatible
  with the existing and future land uses of the applicable zone.
  Pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code (SGMC) Section 11.21.030 “Land use permissions
  tables”, Conditional Use Permits are required to be reviewed and approved for
  “Antenna/Communications Equipment” in the Civic Center zone. The project proposal is
  to install a wireless facility, containing antennas for communications, on the rooftop of an
  existing apartment structure.

  3. Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood.
  Approval of the CUP would not result in detrimental impacts to adjacent properties or to
  the character or function of the neighborhood, as the project proposal does not constitute
  any changes in use or an intensification of use.

  4. The project proposal is exempt from CEQA under Class 3 Categorical Exemption.
  The proposed Conditional Use Permit is Categorically Exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) as a under Class 3 Categorical Exemption pursuant to
  Section 15303 of the CEQA Guidelines. Class 3 consists of construction and location of
  limited numbers of new, small facilities or structures; installation of small new equipment
  and facilities in small structures; and the conversion of existing small structures from one
  use to another where only minor modifications are made in the exterior of the structure.

SUBJECT: RESOLUTION MAKING A DETERMINATION OF PUBLIC
CONVENIENCE OR NECESSITY FOR THE SALE OF BEER AND WINE FOR OFF­
SITE CONSUMPTION FOR THE NEIGHBORHOOD MARKET/CONVENIENCE
STORE, RUBIO'S MARKET, LOCATED AT 10365 CALIFORNIA AVENUE

PURPOSE: To consider a request made by the "Applicant", San Juana Rubio, for the Planning
Commission to make a determination of public convenience or necessity for the sale of beer and
wine for off-site consumption at an existing "Neighborhood Market/Convenience Store" (Rubia's
Market).

RECOMMENDED ACTIONS:

  a. ADOPT Resolution making a determination of public convenience or necessity for the sale
  of beer and wine for off-site consumption for a Neighborhood Market/Convenience Store
  located at 10365 California Avenue;
  b. AUTHORIZE the Department of Community Development to issue a letter of Public
  Convenience or Necessity (PCN) for the "Neighborhood Market/Convenience Store"
  located at 10365 California Avenue.

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: A Legal Notice was not required to be posted, published, or mailed
to the General Public.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: This project is Categorically Exempt from the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) under a Class 1 (Existing Facilities) Categorical
Exemption pursuant to Section 15301, of the State CEQA Guidelines. Class 1 consists of the
operation, repair, maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alterations of existing
public or private structures, facilities, mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving
negligible or no expansion of existing or former use.

ANALYSIS: Staff bas completed a review of the request to grant the Applicant a Public
Convenience or Necessity letter and detennined that making the determination for Public
Convenience and Necessity for the sale of beer and wine will not be detrimental to the public
health or safety.

BACKGROUND: During its regular meeting of September 6, 2022, the City Plaru1ing
Commission conducted a public hearing, as required by law, to consider the approval of
Conditional Use Pem1it No. 862 for the sale of beer and wine at an existing Neighborhood

  24
 Market/Convenience Store located at 10365 California Avenue, which is operated under the name
“Rubio’s Market”. The City’s Planning Commission approved the Conditional Use Permit on a
4/0 vote. Comments were requested from the South Gate Police Department and “No Concerns”
was the response provided.

In order to sell alcohol at Rubio’s Market, the Applicant needs not only the CUP issued by the
City, but also a license (in this case a “Type 20” license) from the California Department of
Alcoholic Beverage Control (“ABC”). In situations where the ABC license is being sought for a
location within in an area designated under state law as having an “undue concentration” of
establishments already licensed to sell alcohol, the ABC must deny the application unless the
applicant qualifies for an exception under Business and Professions Code Section 23958.4. One
of those exceptions is when the local governing body or its designee – in this case, the Planning
Commission – determines that the public convenience or necessity would be served by the ABC’s
issuance of the License. Because the area in which Rubio’s Market is located is not an area of
undue concentration, the Applicant did not request such a determination at the time the CUP was
issued.

Subsequent to the City’s issuance of the CUP, the ABC concluded that it was unable to issue a
Type 20 license to the Applicant because of Section 23817.5 of the Business and Professions Code,
which permanently established a moratorium on the issuance of off-sale beer and wine licenses
(Type 20) in cities and counties where the ratio of Type 20 licenses exceeds one for each 2,500
inhabitants. The “2023 Moratorium Figures” published by the ABC determined that South Gate is
amongst the cities that exceed said ratio. However, the ABC advised the Applicant that the ABC
may still be able to issue a Type 20 license, notwithstanding the moratorium, if the City were to
determine that that public convenience or necessity would be served by the issuance of the Type
20 license. Applicant is requesting that the City make such a determination and issue a letter to
that effect to the ABC, to assist Applicant in her efforts to obtain the Type 20 license.

Site History
The subject property is zoned MS (Main Street) and is located on the northeast corner of California
and Tenaya Avenue (see Figure 1 and Table 1, each on the next page). It sits on a Corridor Overlay
Zone, California (5 Sub Area) and is subject to the development and permit procedures of the City
of South Gate’s General Plan. The CUP issued by the City allows the off-sale of beer and wine at
Rubio’s Market, but subject to specified conditions, one of which is the Applicant’s procurement
of the Type 20 license from the ABC.

 ABC Review
As noted above, alcohol sales will be in accordance with the provisions of a Type 20 (Off-Sale
Beer and Wine) alcohol license as issued by the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage
Control (ABC). Rubio’s Market is located within Census Tract No. 5358.02 (see Figure 2). As
also noted above, based on the records obtained on the AABC’s online website, this census tract
does not have an “undue concentration” of licenses already issued by the ABC, as that term is
defined by Business and Professions Code Section 23958.4(a)(2), which sets a ratio for the
maximum amount of recommended licensed premises. Under the formula set forth by that statute,
a maximum of four (4) on-sale licensed premises are recommended in this census tract, with any
additional licenses constituting an undue concentration. Currently, the census tract holds one (see
Figure 3).
